preview: An interview experience at Goldman Sachs for an internship role detailing the online test, technical rounds, and technical + HR round.
content: Interview Experience Goldman Sachs Hrim Gandhi, B.Tech CS 2018-22 Part 1: Online Test(Aptitude): The online test took place on 27th August 2020. 130-150 students from different branches gave the test. It was conducted on Hackerank and was divided into different sections. Each section had a separate timer, and you weren’t allowed to attempt questions in the previous sections once the timer ran out. It consisted of five sections namely: 1. 2 Coding Questions (35 mins) 2. MCQs, I don’t remember the count. They were based on: PnC and Probability Trigonometry and basic math formulae learned in 11th and 12th Tip: Don’t take MCQs lightly, sometimes they can be a deciding factor for whether you get shortlisted or not. Also there was a negative marking scheme for MCQs, so read the instructions well. 3. MCQs again, based on CS related subjects Computer Networks LRU from OS Programming language related, OOPS Time complexity, recursive functions, dynamic programming 4. Advanced Coding Question (45 mins) 5. 2 Essay type situation based questions Describe a time where your passion and energy led to a team victory. You are in a team of two members, and your co-team member cannot work on the project that needs to be completed within a certain deadline. What will you do in this situation? Tip: Generally no one takes this section seriously, but I would suggest attempting it honestly if you have time for this section. Coding Questions The coding questions were of medium to hard difficulty level. The difficulty of the questions may vary drastically each year. a. Section 1 1. First question was related to finding distance. I don’t remember the question, but it was easily solvable. I passed 11/12 test cases in the first go, and the last test case required us to apply modular arithmetic operation (1e9+7) though it wasn’t mentioned anywhere. Tip: If you fail only a few of the test cases, it might be because of mod. Also in some cases you need to do (ans+mod)%mod instead of ans%mod, these are the cases of overflow. 2. There were two friends Alice and Bob. Bob goes to Alice’s house to play, but one fine day there were trees that fell on his path. Now he has to find the length of shortest path(consider euclidean distance) to reach Alice’s house avoiding the trees. Alice’s and Bob’s house coordinates are given on the XY plane. The coordinates of a tree are given by two points on the XY plane representing the start and the end of the tree. Assume trees to be of the form of line segments on the XY plane and their houses to be like points on the plane. I was able to pass 4/12 test cases. b. Section 4 (Advanced) We were given a n*m matrix with each cell containing a number i, representing i th type of flowers in that cell. We had to find the size of the largest connected component (any cell in the connected component has at least one of its sides common with any other cell of the component ) having at most two different types of flowers. Input: 3 4 1 2 3 1 1 1 2 1 4 2 1 1 Output: 10 The question is similar to the link I have mentioned below. It can be solved using DFS, however I wasn’t able to solve this question in the test. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-number-of-islands/ Tip: Go through questions that you weren’t able to solve or think of an optimal approach for a question that you had solved in the online test. Many times you get a similar question in technical interviews. Also sometimes, the interviewers have a copy of your answers to the online test, and may ask you to explain your approach. Part 2: Technical Interview There were 2 technical interviews which consisted mainly of DSA questions (at least in my case). The interviews were held on a zoom video call, and we were asked to code on Hackerrank Codepair during the interviews. 29 people had been shortlisted for this round. Round 1: Technical My interview started with the basic tell-me-about-yourself question. Tip: This is always going to be the first question in all the interviews you give, so prepare a crisp introduction that you will use everywhere. The things you say can guide your interview from here on. For example, if you say you are more into development, you can expect follow up questions on your projects. Also you can mention your internships, hackathons and positions of responsibility. He then moved to asking me DSA questions: (i) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/search-an-element-in-a-sorted-and-pivoted-array/ (ii) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/lexicographical-maximum-substring-string/ I was asked to code the second question. My code was compiled, and he tested it on multiple test cases. Luckily I didn't get any errors, but even if you get some you can always debug those with a calm mind. The links that I gave above were not the exact same questions but the logic was the same as used to solve the above questions. After this he asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him questions about the work culture at Goldman, the projects that they work on, and what will be my role as an intern. Also I asked him, is there anything in my resume that is a matter of concern. It was beneficial for me as it turned out he had not seen my resume, so after this question he checked my resume as well. Out of 29, 15 were shortlisted for the next round. Round 2: Technical The round as always began with the tell-me-about-yourself question. She asked me to describe any project of my choice. I had done a summer internship, so I described that project. From my resume she also asked me about a hackathon that I had mentioned in achievements. After that we moved to DSA questions: 1. Find the minimum depth of the binary tree. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-minimum-depth-of-a-binary-tree/ 2. Given a source and a destination coordinate on a chessboard, find the minimum number of moves a knight will have to make to reach from the source to the destination. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/minimum-steps-reach-target-knight/ Till here, I was asked to code for both the questions. As the interview was on a zoom call, I had used the whiteboard to explain the logic. Tip: Think out loud. Explain your logic, before you move on to the code. Even if you are stuck on a question, build up your approach and explain as you think. Listen carefully to the interviewer, generally they give you hints when you are stuck somewhere. Having said that, don’t ask for help from your side, tell your approach and work on that. 3. I was given the list of friends of two users on Facebook and was asked to find their mutual friends. As the question didn’t mention the way the data is formatted I asked this, to which she replied that I could use any data structure of my choice. I gave one solution that was using intersection of sets. Another approach I gave was merging of both the lists into a single array of objects. Mutual friends will appear twice, can be found using hashing or sorting and checking consecutive elements. When I gave two to three different solutions, she was satisfied. With this ended my second round. Part 3: Technical + HR Round This round was taken only for 5 people out of the 15. Interview began with introduce-yourself question. This round was conducted by two interviewers, one took the technical section for the first half, followed by the HR interview. In the technical section, I was asked DSA questions as I mentioned in my introduction that I do competitive programming. 1. Given an n*m matrix of 1s and 0s only, where a group of connected 1s forms an island, find the number of islands. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-number-of-islands/ 2. I was given a string s. A rotated string of s is defined as any string r that is made by concatenating two non empty substrings(s1,s2) of s such that s=s1+s2 and r=s2+s1; I gave an O(n^2) solution. More optimal would have been using https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/kmp-algorithm-for-pattern-searching/ After this question, the HR round began. In the beginning, I was asked a few questions on core CS subjects. Questions were based on Computer Networks, Operating Systems, and System Design (the basic scalability question). 1. How familiar are you with Computer Networks ? I said I know only the basics, as we have this course in our current semester. https://medium.com/@maneesha.wijesinghe1/what-happens-when-you-type-an-url-in-the-browser-and-press-enter-bb0aa2449c1a Luckily I had read this article, and I included everything mentioned in this article in my answer. 2. What is memory management in operating systems? Do you know the concept of virtual memory? Explain. 3. Suppose you deploy your website, and the users increase 500x, how would you scale it up? In the end, they asked me if I had any questions for them. Tip: Always ask questions, it shows your interest in the company as well as your communication skills and confidence. I asked a few questions, to which the interviewer gave detailed answers. With that ended the third round. Results The way they selected candidates for the internship was confusing. They selected 2 applicants directly, from 15 who gave the second round (technical), and 4 applicants out of 5 who gave third round (technical + HR). So in total 6 of us (2 girls, 4 boys) were offered the internship. Tip: The key point is to always be prepared for anything and stay calm in between the rounds. You may be called at any moment for your next round, or it may so happen that you get selected without giving the third round. In my case, one hour after my third round, 3 of us were asked to join the zoom call together. It was kind of a prank round, and all three of us were offered the internship. So be patient (or not xD) and enjoy the process. Preparation I used interviewbit.com (one question from each bucket) and geeksforgeeks.com articles for DSA preparation. If you are starting late, it's the best platform. Whenever you are preparing for an interview, reading company specific archives from geeksforgeeks.com and about interview experiences helps a lot. You will get the basic idea of what kind of questions you will be asked and what their domain can be. Different questions about your projects can be asked. You can also be asked many questions on core subjects apart from DSA like OS, DBMS, CN, etc. I was just lucky in that case, because in the majority of rounds I was asked DSA questions. This totally depends on your interviewer and your luck. Lastly, it’s okay to be nervous. It’s okay to not stay calm. But don’t let it affect your interview. Be confident about yourself, and everything shall go well. All the Best!
